upstream.garminconnectReferenceNote: Facade method names and HTTP verbs in this manifest were re-confirmed against garminconnect/__init__.py at 0.3.10. Every facade method the pinned Taxuspt surface reaches still exists there with an identical verb set, so moving the reference from 0.3.8 to 0.3.10 changed no classification in this file.

extraction.method: static AST analysis of the pinned upstream sources with Python's ast module; upstream code was never executed
extraction.script: scratchpad extract.py + gen.py (development-time only; Python is not a runtime or build dependency of this project)
extraction.matchedRegistrations: decorators of the form @app.tool() / @app.resource(<uri>) on functions under src/garmin_mcp

fieldDefinitions.authRequired: Garmin axis. true when invoking this record performs at least one Garmin-authenticated HTTP call, so a valid Garmin session or credential must exist server-side. false means no Garmin call happens at all; it does NOT mean the record is unauthenticated at the MCP layer. Derived statically from whether any garminconnect facade method or raw client call is reachable.
fieldDefinitions.mcpAuthorizationRequired: MCP axis. true when the server requires an authorized MCP caller holding every scope in `scopesRequired` before it dispatches this record. This is true for every tool and resource on the surface, including records with authRequired: false, so there is no anonymous or unscoped entry point. `authRequired: false` together with a non-empty `scopesRequired` is therefore consistent, not contradictory: the scope is enforced by this server, not by Garmin.
fieldDefinitions.scope: The single primary scope gate for the record: the functional domain that owns the object acted on, plus the action implied by the effect class.
fieldDefinitions.scopesRequired: Every scope the caller must hold, all of them and not any of them. Enforced when mcpAuthorizationRequired is true.
fieldDefinitions.idempotency: Whether replaying the call converges on the same end state. A guarantee that depends on a pre-check which fails open is not idempotency: such records are `non-idempotent` and their `idempotencyNote` states the fail-open path and the retry policy.
